notes: Lead's up-front work, not counted in the cost: writing plan v3 (five tasks, seven contracts) and the plan change v4.

Phase 1: Midflight's AI reviewer (Amazon Nova Pro) raised two false alarms. E-5 called 'bookings computes the quote itself' and 'pricing embeds the rate table' a conflict; E-6 said R-4 'doesn't specify how revenue is calculated'. T3 and T4 stopped before writing any code. The lead dismissed both and sent messages 6 and 7.
Phase 2: the lead approved plan v4 in Midflight; nothing was pasted to any agent. Directives went to T2, T3, T4, T5 and none to T1. T2 built the change straight away.

Phase 2: Midflight escalated the cancellation disagreement (E-8, and E-7 for the same question, which also pulled in T5). T3, T4, and T5 stopped. The lead resolved both with request_revision and the fixed decision, then sent messages 13 to 15.

Second round: T3 revised to 'on cancel, total becomes the fee kept'; T4's claim said total stays the amount charged. Midflight caught that mismatch before either wrote code (E-10, a real catch). It also raised E-9 (T3's new 10% against T4's not-yet-revised 20%, a timing artifact) and E-11 (the command line 'prints the total' against 'the API applies a fee', not a conflict). The lead answered all three: total never changes. Messages 16 to 18.

Third round: two more false alarms. E-12 compared two older claim revisions that said the same thing; E-13 said 'gives the hours back' implies the total changes. T5 stopped again. The lead dismissed both and sent message 19.

Totals: 9 escalations, of which 3 were the real disagreement or a real interface mismatch (E-7, E-8, E-10) and 6 were not (E-5, E-6, E-9, E-11, E-12, E-13). The lead acted four times after the plan approval.

C13 failed at merge: the report was empty. Reports read bookings through an in-process function, list_bookings(), that bookings never wrote. Reports had listed that assumption in every claim ('not in the plan contracts; T3 must confirm'). Midflight reviewed four revisions of that claim, approved the last with 'Findings: none', and never told T3. The lead's 10% decision itself was built correctly on both sides.
One fix round: the fixer added list_bookings().
